subjects: Why should I contribute to open source?
dataModel.section_0_heading: Why should I contribute to open source?
dataModel.section_0_points:
• Improve coding skills and learn new technologies.
• Build a public portfolio of your work.
• Network with other developers and experts.
• Gain experience with real-world projects and collaboration workflows.
• Give back to the community and impact projects you use.
• Enhance your resume and career opportunities.
dataModel.section_1_points:
• Finding the right project that matches your skills and interests.
• Understanding a large, unfamiliar codebase.
• Navigating project-specific contribution guidelines and tools.
• Fear of making mistakes or submitting low-quality code.
• Dealing with initial feedback or rejections.
• Time commitment and balancing with other responsibilities.
dataModel.section_2_points:
• Define your interests and skill level.
• Explore projects you already use or are passionate about.
• Look for projects with 'good first issue' or 'help wanted' labels.
• Read the project's `CONTRIBUTING.md` file.
• Start with small contributions like documentation fixes or bug reports.
• Engage with the community on forums or chat channels.

dataModel.title: Your First Steps in Open Source
dataModel.goal:
I want to start contributing to open source. Answer these frequently asked questions so I can open one at a time: why should I contribute, what are the common early challenges, and what are my first steps. Then ask me which of those three topics I want to go deeper on.

dataModel.summary: Your First Steps in Open Source
dataModel.section_0_points:
• Identify what you want to gain (learn a new skill, build a portfolio, solve a problem, network).
• This helps you choose the right projects and maintain momentum.
dataModel.section_1_points:
• Start small: look for projects with 'good first issue' or 'help wanted' tags.
• Consider projects related to technologies you already know or want to learn.
• Look for active communities and clear contribution guidelines.
dataModel.section_2_points:
• Fork the repository to your GitHub account.
• Clone your forked repository to your local machine.
• Follow the project's setup instructions (install dependencies, run tests).
dataModel.section_3_points:
• Start with documentation fixes, typo corrections, or small bug fixes.
• Read the `CONTRIBUTING.md` file for specific guidelines.
• Create a new branch for your changes.
• Commit your changes with a clear message.
• Push your branch to your fork.
• Open a pull request (PR) to the original repository.
dataModel.section_4_points:
• Be responsive to feedback on your PR.
• Be polite and open to suggestions.
• Learn from code reviews and discussions.
